assumptions: Annual time step and closed local community
Trait spread provides drought insurance through facilitation
Pollution adds mortality and habitat loss scales carrying capacity
Scenario parameters are illustrative, not measured

candidate_models.name: stochastic trait-structured competition model
candidate_models.reason: directly represents weather, interactions, traits, and stressors

candidate_models.name: empirical hierarchical state-space model
candidate_models.reason: preferred with longitudinal plot data, unavailable here

data_audit.consequence: Parameters cannot be fitted and predictions cannot be externally validated.

falsification: Reject facilitation mechanism if matched communities show no positive richness-by-drought interaction
Reject tolerance-growth tradeoff if measured growth and drought tolerance are not negatively associated
Reject viability threshold if out-of-sample survival ranking is not better than richness-neutral baseline
Reformulate if time-step refinement changes qualitative rankings

math_specification.adaptation: A_i increases under drought and relaxes toward baseline tolerance otherwise
math_specification.state: B_i(t)>=0 biomass and A_i(t) in [tau_i,0.99] adaptation
math_specification.viability: mean biomass over final 20 years and survival if all final-20 annual totals >=0.05
math_specification.weather: D_t~Bernoulli(p); W_t is bounded stochastic water adequacy conditional on D_t

problem_framing.objective: Explain how interacting plant communities respond over time to irregular drought, richness, composition, drought regime, pollution, and habitat loss.

reviewer_risks: Benefit threshold depends on preregistered 5% rule
Competition matrix reduced to one coefficient
No spatial dispersal or seed bank

sensitivity_robustness.limitation: does not identify joint interactions or parameter posterior uncertainty
sensitivity_robustness.method: one-at-a-time three-level sweeps with identical seed schedule

validation.external: pending: no empirical observations in benchmark
